studies.Reference: Vitamin D and reduced risk of breast cancer: a population-based case-control study.
studies.Authors: Knight JA, Lesosky M, Barnett H, Raboud JM, Vieth R
studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Telephone interviews were completed for 972 cases and 1,135 controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Reduced risk was also associated with cod liver oil use
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Women with newly diagnosed invasive breast cancer were identified from the Ontario Cancer Registry.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 759 cases and 1,135 controls from a case-control study (Ontario, Canada, 2003-2005)
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: increased intake of vitamin D (from the sun and diet) was most consistently associated with a significantly reduced risk of ER+/PR+ tumors
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: association between vitamin D intake at specific ages and combined estrogen-receptor- (ER) and progesterone-receptor- (PR) defined breast cancer
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: use of cod liver oil during adolescence

headline.funnel_interpretation: Insufficient studies to perform formal publication bias testing.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.68–0.9), suggesting that cod liver oil is associated with a lower risk of breast cancer. These findings were supported by low between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.
